title: Why Do Airplane Windows Have a Tiny Hole?

lines.text: Ever noticed this tiny hole in an airplane window?
That window is actually three panes stacked together.
And the hole is drilled in the middle pane, not the outer one.
Up high, cabin air is pressurized, but the air outside is thin.
The hole lets cabin air reach the gap between the panes, so the outer pane takes most of the pressure difference.
That keeps the middle pane fresh as a backup, and it lets moisture out so your window stays clear.
